uncited: The method operates as an iterative loop to generate aligned training and testing data.
*   *Note:* The rendered images are often blurry due to misalignment, which violates the general optical flow assumption of sharp paired inputs.
The warping aligns the ground truth content with the geometry estimated by the NeRF.
*   **Memory Constraints:** PWC-Net may run out of memory on high-resolution images.
*   **Blurry Inputs:** NeRF rendered images are often blurry due to misalignment, violating the sharp-pair assumption of optical flow estimators.
*   **Time Complexity:** The method requires multiple iterations of NeRF training and optical flow estimation.
Each iteration involves rendering all training views, running PWC-Net, and warping images.
*   **Memory Complexity:** High memory usage due to the need to store and process high-resolution images and optical flow fields.
It was developed to address the issue of misalignment in NeRF training, particularly in the context of the mip-NeRF 360 dataset.
The authors observed that standard NeRF training with inaccurate poses leads to blurry renders, which in turn hampers the accuracy of optical flow estimation if used for alignment.
The iterative approach was proposed to break this cycle by progressively aligning the training data.
